narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Sound of Saudade: Dancing the Morna
This is morna. 18th to 20th century.
on_screen: Hero video, first 10 seconds (aN8KsbFz3jE)
Title card: morna · Cape Verde · 18th to 20th century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The morna originated in the 18th century on Boa Vista Island.
It is believed to be a cross between the lundum and the choros.
In the early 20th century, Eugénio Tavares introduced a more romantic and lyrical style in Brava.
on_screen: Map: Cape Verde · Africa
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The morna is performed at key life events such as weddings, christenings, and family reunions.
It is a symbol of national identity, reflecting themes of saudade, love, departure, and the sea.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: File:Morna Sodade na Praia Branca.webm (https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/1b/Morna_Sodade_na_Praia_Branca.webm?utm_source=commons.wikimedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=original)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The morna is a ballroom dance performed in pairs.
Dancers embrace their partner with one arm and hold hands with the other.
The movement consists of two body swings to one side per bar, with the direction of the swing alternating every bar.
Watch for Body sway.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (aN8KsbFz3jE)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Pairs, ballroom style.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is typically lento with a binary meter.
Traditional instrumentation includes the guitar (violão), cavaquinho, violin (rabeca), piano, clarinet, and accordion.
Listen for the guitar, cavaquinho, violin, piano.
The pulse is 2/4 or 4/4 at about 60 beats a minute.
A slow, acoustic sound characterized by the interplay of guitar arpeggios and melodic solo instruments like the violin, conveying a sense of deep longing.
on_screen: Instrument names on screen as each is mentioned
Listen later: Rabilona — Teté Alhinho; Força di cretcheu — Celina Pereira; Voz — Tété Alhinho (2005)
Waveform or rhythm-pattern graphic: Syncopated, with the melody accentuated on the first beat and the last half-beat of the bar.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Cesária Évora, Eugénio Tavares, B. Leza, Bana, and Fantcha.
Boa Vista morna (quicker tempo, rubato style), Brava morna (slower tempo, romanticism, rigid meter), and São Vicente morna (enriched chord sequences with passing chords).
The morna is related to the lundum and the choros, and shares cultural connections with the Portuguese fado, Brazilian modinha, and Argentine tango.

music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of morna (Cape Verde). Meter 2/4 or 4/4. Tempo about 60 bpm. Rhythm pattern: Syncopated, with the melody accentuated on the first beat and the last half-beat of the bar.. Instruments: guitar, cavaquinho, violin, piano, clarinet, accordion. Vocal style: Emotive, lyrical, often in Cape Verdean Creole.. Form: Strophes alternating with a refrain.. Mood: melancholic, romantic, plaintive. It should sound like this: A slow, acoustic sound characterized by the interplay of guitar arpeggios and melodic solo instruments like the violin, conveying a sense of deep longing.
